facts.claim: With computer use, Claude doesn’t connect to the computer itself: your application receives its requests, turns them into clicks and keystrokes, captures the results such as screenshots, and sends them back.
Repeating the request, the action and the returned screenshot without user input is what Anthropic calls the agent loop.
For web applications Anthropic suggests a display of 1280 × 800 or 1366 × 768, and advises against going above 1920 × 1080.
Coordinates are in screenshot pixels: if you scale screenshots down before sending them, scale Claude’s coordinates back up before clicking on the real display.
Some applications need time to respond to actions; Anthropic’s example pauses after each click so the screen can update, and the tool has a wait action for pages still loading.
Claude sometimes acts as if an action succeeded without checking; Anthropic suggests prompting it to take a screenshot after each step and check the outcome.
Claude sometimes follows commands found in content even when they conflict with your instructions: instructions on web pages or in images might override yours.
Classifiers scan what the computer-use tools return, such as screenshots, to flag likely prompt injections; Anthropic says the other precautions remain important even so.
Anthropic advises limiting the computer’s internet access to an allow-list of domains, to reduce exposure to malicious content.
Anthropic advises asking a person to confirm decisions with real-world consequences and anything needing consent, such as completing a payment or agreeing to terms of service.
Anthropic advises running computer use in a dedicated virtual machine or container with minimal privileges, and keeping sensitive data such as logins out of the model’s reach.
Claude reads images in 28 × 28-pixel patches, one visual token each, so a screenshot costs ⌈width / 28⌉ × ⌈height / 28⌉ tokens.
OSWorld (Xie et al., 2024) is a benchmark of 369 computer tasks in real web and desktop apps: people completed 72.36% of them, the best model at the time 12.24%.
Steel’s OSWorld leaderboard, last updated 11 October 2026, lists several agents above the paper’s 72.36% human baseline, the highest at 86.1%; third-party boards disagree on the leader.
In January 2025 OpenAI reported that its Computer-Using Agent, which sees the screen as pixels and acts with a mouse and keyboard, completed 38.1% of OSWorld tasks, then the best score.
